== Biography ==
Sarah was born about 1790. She is the daughter of William C Patterson Jr and Agnes (Patton) Patterson.

Sally was named in the 1824 will of her father, William C Patterson (see his profile for a transcript of the will). Her father indicated that he had already gifted Sally and her husband, William Glasgow, all they were entitled.

In June 1829, William Glasgow and his wife, Sally, sold 190 acres of land in Wythe County on Reed Creek to Stephen Sayers for $1,050.<ref>
'''Indenture''': Deed Book 11, 1828-1831, Wythe County, Virginia:;
"#008562846"<br/>
 > image 183 of 363<br/>
{{FamilySearch Image|3Q9M-C3QP-NQ82-5}} (accessed 10 September 2025)
</ref>

Sally was also named as a legatee in the 1840 will of her mother, Agnes Patterson.<ref>

In 1850, William (62) and Sarah (60) Glasgow lived in Pulaski County, Virginia with their 23-year-old daughter, Louisa. William was employed as a laborer.<ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Original 1829 deed review ===

Original image 183 of DGS 008562846 was downloaded through the authorized viewer and read 24 October 2026. William Glasgow and Sally his wife convey 190 acres on Reed Creek, a branch of New River, Wythe County, to Stephen Sayers for $1,050. Boundaries name Isaac Brown and John Craig. Both Glasgow spouses sign/seal. James Graham and Jacob Haller certify 14 December 1829; both acknowledgments describe the deed as 8 June 1829. The opening day is faint; the earlier biography’s 3 June 1829 is retained as a date discrepancy rather than silently harmonized. Recorded 12 January 1830. The complete entry contains no named Glasgow kin, inherited-title recital or acquisition history.<ref name="WytheDeed1829">Wythe County, Virginia, Deed Book 11, 1828–1831 (supplied citation), DGS 008562846,[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-C3QP-NQ82-5 image 183], complete original conveyance and acknowledgments visually checked 24 October 2026. Both acknowledgments say 8 June 1829; the opening day is faint and an earlier account gives 3 June. Recorded 12 January 1830. No parent or inherited-title clause.</ref>

Her husband [[Glasgow-3678|William Glasgow]] now has a possible biologicalfather hypothesis,[[Glasgow-1543|Joseph Glasgow]], 30%. The will’s William may instead be [[Glasgow-563|William Glasgow]], Joseph’s nephew; no literal biological parent clause has been found. This does not reassess Sally’s own parents or her children’s maternal attachments.
